title: One fixed read-aloud pace, with replay
statement: Read text aloud at one fixed pace set for the grade, not per learner, and let learners pause and replay rather than slowing the voice, which distorts speech.
example: For grade 3 the pace is 110 to 120 words a minute, with no per-student speed.
detail: A model lesson sheet for a grade 3 reading course sets the read-aloud at a fixed pace with no per-student speed, and a review call gave the reason as one standardised, age-appropriate reading speed across all lessons. A later call accepted the argument that slowing audio distorts prosody, breaks sentence continuity and compromises fidelity, so learners should pause and replay at the set pace, and the build lets a child tap a line the voice has already reached to hear it again (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/audio-and-voiceover.md`, lines 73-89). The same call kept a slower option for struggling readers, and the course records the earlier no-speed-control decision as superseded but never withdrawn.
against: The course kept a slower option: "'slow enough' is highly subjective, noting that struggling readers or children with special educational needs require a slightly dialed-down pace" (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/audio-and-voiceover.md`, lines 272-274), and "The settlement was normal-and-slower, which is what the repo implements" (line 276), with exactly two speeds, `normal` at 1x and `slower` at 0.85x (lines 49-51). A later handover judged the faster course-wide playback rate a real variance from the specification with no demonstrated harm, and found no words-per-minute figure in the updated procedure document (`grade3-reading/_archive/handovers/HANDOVER-2026-09-24.md`, lines 255 and 262). For teens, a Grade 9 design guide gives learners speed control instead: "Let students skip or speed up audio." (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/learners-voice-guide.md`, line 94).
